text:
claire_support: FYI — Customer (Acme corp) reports JSON mode streaming responses getting cut off mid-object. They get a parse error client-side.

john_acme: repro attached. We call /v1/generate?mode=structured with SSE. Last chunk ends with \"...,\\n  \"metadata\": {\"id\": \"abc123\"\" and then connection closes. Parser throws unexpected EOF.

claire_support: They provided this curl to reproduce:
```
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\ \\n  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?mode=structured&model=rwd-3-small\"
```

ben_support: thanks — can you paste raw response tail?

john_acme: here's the tail from our client capture (note missing closing braces):
```
data: {\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{\"content\":\"{\\\"items\\\":[\\\"a\\\",\\\"b\\\",\\\"c\\\"]\\\",\\\"metadata\\\":{\\\"id\\\":\\\"abc123\\\"\"\n
```

claire_support: reproable on our side? sam_runtime?

sam_runtime: looking. I see a request id X-Req-Id=req-7b2f in the logs. At ~t+18s the connection FINs from the edge. The server had sent ~12 chunks; last chunk is partial 128 bytes.

maya_infra: checking edge traces (CF/ALB). Cloudfront log shows \"origin: 504 Gateway Timeout\" for the req-7b2f call, but our origin (nginx upstream) returned 200 earlier. There's a chunked transfer that seems to be cut when keepalive stalls.

sam_runtime: interesting — we reproduce locally by running a stress SSE stream (large JSON array emitted across many chunks) and forcing upstream read_timeout=10s. The stream can be cut mid-chunk if the client or proxy closes the TCP stream during a flush.

ben_support: customer says this started after they switched to production Cloudflare in front of their client. Could CF be trimming trailing chunk?

maya_infra: CF sometimes upgrades to HTTP/2 and changes chunking behavior. If client or intermediary doesn't read remaining bytes before TLS close, you can see incomplete JSON. There's also a known ALB idle timeout of 60s.

claire_support: immediate ask to customer: can you run curl with --no-buffer and capture raw tcpdump? Also try connecting with curl -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" -N to see if it keeps the socket open.

john_acme: we'll capture and send pcap. We reproduced 1/3 times.

sam_runtime: for our priority: add a defensive framing layer in structured-mode that emits a final \"end_of_object\" sentinel event OR guarantees last chunk contains the closing bracket in a single flush. Short-term we can also update docs to recommend chunked flush semantics and using Content-Length for non-streaming.

ben_support: opening INC-4567 and assigning to eng-runtime. Tagging eng-infra for proxy traces.

deploy-bot: Created issue INC-4567: \"SSE structured output partial-chunk EOF causing parser errors\" assigned to sam_runtime, priority P2, due 2026-03-20.

sam_runtime: repro steps (local) — node SSE server used to emulate large array: 
```js
// minimal repro server
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req,res)=>{
  res.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache'});
  res.write('data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"[');
  // simulate many small writes
  for(let i=0;i<500;i++){
    res.write(`data: ${JSON.stringify(i)},\n`);
  }
  // flush but don't send closing brace to simulate mid-chunk loss
  setTimeout(()=>res.end(),15000);
}).listen(5600);
```

sam_runtime: when a proxy or client resets during that 15s window, the last event can be truncated. Our streaming parser on SDKs treats SSE frames atomically, but if the final SSE data field contains partial JSON we get parse errors.

maya_infra: workaround: enable TCP keepalives and lower idle timeouts for path /v1/generate for customers with structured mode heavy streams. Also add a probe heartbeat event every 5s to avoid long idle windows.

ben_support: customer asked for ETA for a fix. What's realistic?

sam_runtime: short-term (48h) — doc + heartbeat + recommend proxy rules. Medium-term (2 weeks) — server-side change to emit a final sentinel event and make SDK parser more tolerant (buffer until full JSON or timeout).

claire_support: I'll update the customer: propose heartbeat + pcap + doc changes as immediate mitigation, and say engineering will push the sentinel change in ~2 weeks.

john_acme: thanks — will send pcap and confirm whether they see improvement with heartbeat.

ben_support: assigning follow-ups: INC-4567 will collect customer pcap, edge logs, and include repro payload. Leaving thread open until sentinel rollout. :eyes:
